interpretation: SELECTIVE DEFICIT as preregistered: pomaze delta +2.200 > delayed_reward delta +0.046. Episodic memory is causally load-bearing on the partial-observability task.
limitations: DisabledStore also removes the per-action error signal used by the AI selector's IG term (falls back to the running table), so the ablation covers the store's full causal footprint. 3 seeds; affect='none' isolates the world model.

preregistered.ablation: arch_b memory_enabled=False: DisabledStore — no encoding, no retrieval correction, per-action error prediction returns None (selector falls back to its running table).
preregistered.decision_rule: Selective deficit (pomaze seed-mean delta > 0 and > delayed_reward seed-mean delta) -> memory earns a causal role. Seed-mean deltas ≈ 0 on both tasks -> memory decorative in B (NR-B-007).
preregistered.hypothesis: Disabling episodic memory produces a SELECTIVE deficit: pomaze (partial observability; recall should aid revisit-avoidance via retrieval correction) degrades more than delayed_reward (credit flows through the reward-channel learning path).
preregistered.metric: mean_return per task; per-seed delta = intact − no_memory; seed-mean deltas compared across tasks.
preregistered.null: Disabling memory changes nothing on either task — the EpisodicStore is decorative in Architecture B.
preregistered.procedure: Closed-loop runs: pomaze 15 episodes, delayed_reward 10 episodes; affect='none' (world-model isolation); action_mode='active_inference'; identical primary seeds for both conditions (paired).
